## W4: Holographic Clock Display
### The prototype

I went with a much simpler (hopefully!) design this week because of exams!

This session was spent building prototypes for my holographic display.

Pepper's Ghost visual effects are created by securing a thin piece of transparent material at a 45° angle on top of a screen. This allows a viewer to see what is displayed on the screen without seeing the surface itself.

There are two ways I could have implemented this in my design, and I wanted to sus out each option:

* Using an inverted square pyramid, with a seperate image on each face. This creates a 3D-effect
* Using a single tilted piece of glass. This better utilises the whole surface of the underlying display

### The inverted square pyramid prototype

I started by scoring a large piece of acrylic into small, triangle shaped pieces (this took wayyyy too long!!!):

![IMG_8470 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/b28f652b21025924c43b8e6e3ea4196480502fdd1d2eeedf49ae62f7904bb337.jpg)

![IMG_8471 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/63345f23bf464f69c0ccacde8c0fea6806417b2c1f04ec291740a774b6f414dd.jpg)

I then assembled the pyramid:

![IMG_8476 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/96cc72b7bf00b181a9c15765efa8076a4a66e1a8918eebca2e4a446a01a825cc.jpg)

I then used a jellyfish image to test my prototype (sorry about the blurry image).

![IMG_8474 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/e19f8a2de129a312e7097c171cf8408993b8b7ee161b9cd516574eda46cec511.jpg)

The advantage of this is that each edge of the pyramid can have its own image, giving a 3D effect. However, the need for 4 seperate displays, or 1 much larger display, could complicate the PCB design.

### The tilted glass prototype

This prototype was much simpler. After scoring the acrylic sheet into an 8x8cm square, I arrived at the following:

![IMG_8478 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/c0c28bcc51db1125b9041e6edd03484a7b2349a15259ad851adc2d42400b5a32.jpg)

The jellyfish is still visible even as the screen gets much further away, as long as it's directly above:

![IMG_8479 Large](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/3Z57nO3DOx0C7tgaKyZzjKBiZIWIGXGt/30bb674e3e7631087a6f85c5ee1b288af0a48db414e02208c2ca9697f7c1e6bb.jpg)

The advantage of this is it makes PCB and casing design much simpler, while only allowing one viewing angle.

### The verdict

I decided to go with the pyramid, as it will allow me to better create 3D effects and feel more polished as a project.

Next up is selecting parts, then schematic and PCB design, casing, and firmware!

Thanks for reading :)
